review_requirements: Use command history in the interactive shell, execute an external command, and verify the parent terminal remains usable after exit.
Explain how the shell acquires its controlling terminal and why unused PTY descriptors must be closed.
Use vim insert mode and shell arrow keys; verify immediate input and no double echo.
Explain which terminal is made raw and which layer interprets control characters.
Exercise an internal client error and all supported catchable termination signals; compare terminal settings and verify typing, Backspace and Enter after each exit path.
Document SIGKILL limitations and the terminal recovery command.
Resize vim, less or htop repeatedly and rapidly; verify redraw and client responsiveness.
Explain SIGWINCH delivery to foreground process groups and resize-event coalescing.
Inspect PID, PGID, SID and TPGID while a foreground job runs, stops, resumes with bg and returns with fg; verify the shell remains interactive.
Explain how Ctrl+C reaches the foreground job and why pipelines use process groups.
Show distinct machine-readable identities for two active sessions and verify invalid names cannot create files outside the runtime directory.
Explain the authoritative session identity and how uniqueness is enforced atomically.
Inspect the process tree after the creating client exits; identify the PTY master owner, the live command, and the process responsible for reaping it.
Document the detach sequence, literal-prefix escape, prefix wait policy and handling of partial or interrupted sequences.
List one session and several sessions with supported safe punctuation or spaces; verify stable ordering or document that ordering is not guaranteed.
Explain how session discovery distinguishes live sessions from stale metadata.
Kill an idle shell, a shell with a foreground job, and a shell with job-control background children; verify no managed descendants remain.
Document graceful shutdown, forced-termination timeout, repeat-kill behaviour and the process ownership boundary.
On a fresh runtime, launch concurrent first clients and identify the single active coordinator that owns the control socket; prove no conflicting coordinators remain.
Explain startup arbitration, stale PID files and the kernel operation that establishes ownership.
Log invalid UTF-8 and binary bytes and verify the documented rendering policy.
Document whether logs are raw PTY bytes or reconstructed text, and how terminal control sequences are handled.
Inspect ownership and modes of every actual runtime directory, socket and session file; verify command environment and output are not exposed unnecessarily.
Explain rejection or safe repair of unsafe pre-existing paths, including validation/opening races.
Run protocol-decoder fuzzing and record the target, duration, corpus and result.
Run detach-prefix parser fuzzing and record the target, duration, corpus and result.
Stress repeated attach/detach and concurrent list/create/kill operations.
Exercise disconnect during output, kill during attach, coordinator restart during create, writer disconnect during handover, resize during detach and child exit during replay.
Explain deterministic orchestration, readiness conditions and any remaining flaky tests.
